case.title: Coordinating practice in a volunteer language circle
case.beneficiary: Adult participants in a free conversational language circle and the volunteers who coordinate weekly practice.
case.valued_outcome: Participants obtain useful speaking practice at their current level and can prepare for the next session without excessive coordination effort.
case.success_measure: Over six sessions, at least 80% of attending participants report ten or more minutes of useful speaking practice, at least 85% correctly identify their next preparation task, and volunteer coordination stays below 90 minutes per week.

hard_constraints_with_source.text: Participation remains free, and no learner may be excluded for missing a prior session or declining to disclose a proficiency label publicly.
The circle has one room for 75 minutes each Wednesday and no additional paid facilitator time.
Participants must be able to obtain preparation information without a smartphone or personal online account.
The group’s purpose remains conversational practice; success may not be substituted with formal examination scores or completion of unrelated assignments.

changeable_assumptions: The same topic sheet is currently distributed to everyone regardless of previous attendance.
Participants choose their conversation partners after a whole-group opening activity.
case.incumbent_description: A volunteer selects a weekly topic, prints prompts, and sends an optional group message. After introductions, participants practice in pairs and later share a short exchange with the room.

supplied_observations.text: Attendance over six sessions was 18, 11, 21, 15, 12, and 20. Nine people attended at least five sessions; 17 attended only once or twice.
Anonymous exit slips from 72 attendances reported ten useful speaking minutes on 49 occasions; 14 slips reported fewer, and nine left that question blank.
Forty-eight of the 72 slips named the intended next preparation task. Twelve named an earlier task, and twelve supplied no task.
Volunteer coordination took between 70 and 135 minutes per week, including printing, answering messages, choosing topics, and arranging room access.
In two sessions, pair formation took eight and 13 minutes. Four participants changed partners after the first prompt in each session.
Seven frequent attendees described the repeated session structure as helpful. Five occasional attendees reported difficulty entering a conversation already familiar to their partner.
The volunteer counted nine participants who regularly used printed information only. Speaking time was not directly timed, and exit slips were not linked across weeks.

unmeasured_variables: Participants’ definitions of useful practice and the distribution of speaking time within pairs.
Reasons for irregular attendance and time spent on each coordination activity.
available_resources: Two volunteers who alternate weeks, a printer, existing topic sheets, movable chairs, and permission for anonymous session observation.
case.evidence_provenance: authored synthetic case; observations stipulated not real empirical data

raw_candidates.claim: Unequal familiarity with the conversation, rather than proficiency mismatch alone, may explain some difficult pair starts.
raw_candidates.delta: Retain the valued session structure while testing whether a shared starting point improves entry for occasional attendees.
raw_candidates.prediction: Pairs using a fresh, self-contained prompt and brief mutual introduction will start reciprocal speaking sooner and report more useful practice, especially where prior topic familiarity differs.
raw_candidates.probe: Within a session, randomly offer consenting pairs either the usual prompt or a fresh self-contained equivalent with a one-minute introduction. Privately record topic familiarity without proficiency labels; anonymously observe time to reciprocal speaking and each partner's speaking minutes, then collect usefulness reports. Keep both activities inside 75 minutes and record volunteer preparation time.
assumptions: Equivalent prompts can be prepared within the weekly coordination ceiling.
Familiarity can be reported privately; unequal proficiency and prompt differences remain alternative explanations.

raw_candidates.claim: Some preparation errors may reflect confusion between current and earlier task information.
raw_candidates.delta: Test task identification at paper handoff before attributing errors to irregular attendance or motivation.
raw_candidates.prediction: A clearly dated paper card naming the next session and one preparation task will reduce earlier-task answers relative to the existing presentation.
raw_candidates.probe: Give consenting attendees the same next task in either existing format or a reusable dated-card format. Ask privately which task and session it refers to; correct every misunderstanding and provide the dated information to everyone afterward. Count earlier-task and blank answers separately and log printing, explanation, and message time.
assumptions: Immediate identification may not predict later recall.
The card is available without an account and does not make preparation a condition of participation.

raw_candidates.claim: A self-calibrating conversation could let partners use different amounts of support while discussing the same fresh prompt, without declaring proficiency or relying on previous attendance.
raw_candidates.delta: Speculative capability: continuously adjust each person's conversational challenge. Dependencies: accessible entry prompts, independently usable scaffolds, turn allocation, and a reliable signal that challenge remains useful. Presently testable partial capability: reuse existing sheets with optional sentence starters and extension prompts; alternate speaker roles for two six-minute turns before jointly choosing whether to change support.
raw_candidates.prediction: If unequal entry difficulty or turn allocation contributes to low usefulness, the supported rounds should increase both partners' reported useful minutes and reduce the within-pair speaking-time gap. Unchanged usefulness despite more balanced speech would weaken that explanation.
raw_candidates.probe: Within a session, alternate the order of usual and supported rounds across pairs using comparable fresh prompts. Anonymous observation records each partner's speaking time; brief round slips record useful minutes and entry difficulty. Log preparation time and include it in weekly coordination totals.
assumptions: Scaffolds can be adapted within existing volunteer time.
Participants can select support without public proficiency labels.
Balanced speaking does not necessarily mean useful practice.

raw_candidates.claim: An attendance-independent preparation packet could make the next task recoverable after missed sessions through calendar dates alone.
raw_candidates.delta: Speculative capability: preserve preparation continuity without tracking learners. Dependencies: a stable six-session topic sequence, self-contained tasks, unambiguous dates, and printed distribution. Testable partial capability: provide six dated, detachable preparation cards made from existing topics, with spare packets available at every session.
raw_candidates.prediction: If stale task information contributes to errors, dated packets should specifically reduce naming an earlier task; persistent blank answers would suggest an additional barrier.
raw_candidates.probe: Ask participants to identify the next task using the current sheet and the dated packet, counterbalancing order. Record earlier-task errors separately from blanks. Then track task identification across six sessions, counting packet creation, printing and replacement effort toward the weekly 90-minute limit.
assumptions: Topics can be fixed six sessions ahead.
Participants retain packets or obtain a replacement.
No preparation or prior attendance becomes an entry requirement.

case.title: Small museum audio handset return
case.beneficiary: Visitors borrowing audio handsets and the reception attendant
case.valued_outcome: Visitors receive a ready handset with their selected language at the beginning of a visit.
case.success_measure: At least 95% of handoffs during the stipulated entrance period begin playback in the requested language within one minute.

hard_constraints.text: Use the existing twelve handsets and charging dock.
The reception attendant retains responsibility for admission; no added staff.
Do not collect visitor identities or persist listening histories.
Return handling must average no more than 30 seconds per handset.

case.incumbent: Returned handsets enter the charging dock and are handed out when their charge indicator is green. Existing partial mechanisms are green charge indicators showing battery readiness and laminated language cards helping visitors select the handset menu. The attendant relies on the preceding visitor's menu state until the next handoff.

observations.text: Synthetic handoff log: nine of 36 green-indicator handsets initially played the preceding visitor's language.
Synthetic timing record: eight of those nine handoffs exceeded one minute.
Synthetic return sample: checking charge alone took an average of eight seconds per handset.
Synthetic visitor tally: language choices were split among three menu options.
Synthetic menu trial: selecting a language from the home screen took 12 to 22 seconds in six trials.
Synthetic dock audit: four green-indicator handsets were sitting on a language submenu rather than the home screen.

unknowns: Whether submenu state contributes independently to delays.
How return timing overlaps with admission queues.
resources: Existing handsets, charging dock, language cards and timing sheet.
changeable_assumptions: Menu state is handled only at the next handoff.
case.provenance: Entirely authored synthetic preservation fixture; supplied sources are stipulations, not field observations or tested effects.

raw_candidates.claim: A return-to-home-screen step coupled with a visitor language choice before handoff could remove inherited language state and shorten menu navigation.
raw_candidates.delta: Treat menu readiness and requested language as joint handoff conditions alongside battery readiness.
raw_candidates.prediction: If inherited menu state causes delays, the pair may outperform resetting alone or advance choice alone; effects remain untested.
raw_candidates.probe: Compare paired steps, each step alone and existing practice across matched language requests. Stop if return handling exceeds 30 seconds on average.
assumptions: Reset returns reliably to the home screen.
Choice can be communicated without retaining visitor data.

raw_candidates.claim: Language-specific dock positions plus a visible menu-state check might reduce wrong-language handoffs by aligning location cues with actual settings.
raw_candidates.delta: Use location and verified setting together instead of charge indication as the availability cue.
raw_candidates.prediction: If location cues remain accurate, the pair may outperform dock grouping alone; uneven language demand could erase the benefit.
raw_candidates.probe: Compare paired steps with grouping alone under equal and uneven demand. Stop if admission work is delayed or visitor history is retained.
assumptions: Dock positions can be marked without replacement.
Setting checks do not consume admission capacity.

case.valued_outcome: Seat a wooden rail flush without bruising its visible edge.
hard_constraints: No contact with the visible varnished face
Tool travel must remain inside a 35 mm recess
resources: A recess geometry sketch is assumed for the hypothetical case
No tool or workpiece is supplied
Whether a suitable replaceable contact sleeve can be fabricated is unknown

raw_candidates.claim: A guided short-stroke sliding mass might seat the rail within the recess.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: The proposal attributes seating to repeated axial impulses and face protection to a stop referencing an unvarnished surface.
raw_candidates.discriminator: Its prediction is less lateral drift than the flexure striker under identical alignment errors; superiority is unknown. A varnish strike or failure to seat defeats this proposal.
raw_candidates.probe: Proposed only: compare drift and seating on sacrificial geometries with deliberate alignment offsets; inspect all contact marks.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Stop positioning and sufficient impulse within the travel limit remain untested.

raw_candidates.claim: A bent flexure carrying a sleeved head might redirect a hand impulse onto the rail.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: Elastic storage is predicted to concentrate the short input stroke at the rail contact.
raw_candidates.discriminator: The author predicts adequate seating where the short-slide stalls, while expecting worse aim. Failure to seat or visible-face contact defeats that prediction.
raw_candidates.probe: Proposed only: establish whether the indispensable sleeve can be made, then compare seating and aim on a surrogate.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Sleeve availability and flexure fatigue are unknown. This does not request relaxation of any hard constraint.

raw_candidates.claim: A conventional longer swinging head could provide a larger impulse.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: More travel is predicted to permit more impact speed.
raw_candidates.discriminator: Parked as rejected because its proposed travel exceeds 35 mm, even if it seats the rail. Whether it would bruise the edge is unresolved.
raw_candidates.probe: No in-case trial proposed; any later surrogate study would retain the travel violation.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Potential seating benefit and surface damage remain unknown despite rejection.

openings.discriminator: Across matched language requests, compare paired steps, reset alone, advance choice alone and incumbent practice; superiority of the pair distinguishes the proposed joint effect.
openings.probe: Time returns and requested-language playback. Stop if return handling averages over 30 seconds; check reset reliability and its effect on charge indication. Require at least 95% playback within one minute during the stipulated entrance period.
openings.uncertainty: Untested synthetic proposal. Reliable home reset and choice communication without retained visitor data are assumptions; submenu contribution and admission-queue overlap remain unknown.

openings.claim: Mark language-specific positions on the existing dock and visibly verify menu settings alongside charge; location cues could reduce wrong-language handoffs only while they accurately represent settings.
openings.discriminator: Compare grouping plus verification against grouping alone under equal and uneven language demand; demand imbalance could erase the paired benefit.
openings.probe: Measure correct-language handoffs, return time and admission delay. Stop for delayed admission, retained listening history or returns averaging over 30 seconds; verify marking requires no dock replacement.
openings.uncertainty: Effects untested; feasible markings and checks that preserve admission capacity are assumptions. Uneven demand may defeat grouping.
